44.7% of Starlink Speedtest users in the U.S. are now meeting the FCC's official definition of broadband: 100 Mbps download and 20 Mbps upload simultaneously.

In Q1 2025 that number was 17.4%.

In three quarters, Starlink more than doubled the share of its users hitting the broadband standard.

This matters because FCC broadband designation affects federal funding, infrastructure investment and how ISPs are classified and regulated.

Starlink isn't trying to be a satellite workaround. It is becoming a broadband utility.

Starlink now delivers 100 Mbps or higher median download speeds in 49 out of 50 U.S. states.

In 2H 2024, that number was 23 states.

In one year, Starlink went from hitting the 100 Mbps threshold in under half the country to almost all of it.

Source: Ookla Speedtest, 2H 2025 data.

Tesla is going all-in on Europe!

Tesla is pouring nearly $250 million into its Berlin Gigafactory (Grünheide) to skyrocket battery production from 8 GWh to 18 GWh annually. 

This is part of a bigger $1.2 billion expansion that will also add over 1,500 new jobs. Local battery manufacturing means faster EV production, lower logistics costs, and stronger supply chains for the European market. 

Tesla is doubling down on the future of electric vehicles. 
What do you think, smart move or too aggressive?

NEWS: A Tesla Cybercab was spotted with what appears to be a Starlink antenna mounted on the rear.

If that’s really Starlink hardware, it could point toward always-connected autonomous vehicles with direct satellite communication capabilities.

For robotaxis, reliable connectivity matters. Navigation updates, remote diagnostics, fleet coordination and real-time data all depend on staying online.

Interesting detail and definitely something to watch closely.

Tesla passes bright light testing with strong performance.

The system handled intense lighting conditions successfully, an important step for camera-based driving and safety systems that need to operate reliably in the real world.

Harsh sunlight, glare and sudden brightness changes are some of the toughest conditions for vision-based autonomy, making tests like this especially important for FSD development.
